title: Labels are applied where the reporter may set them
iWant: rcf-feedback plus severity:<...> plus area:<...> labels applied by the tool when the destination repo carries them and the reporter has push or triage access
soThat: triage queues sort correctly for reporters who have the right, while outside reporters on a public repo still land readable issues (title prefix and body fingerprint remain the load-bearing handles).

acceptanceCriteria.description: Before create, the tool calls gh label list --json name on the destination repo and intersects the requested labels ("rcf-feedback", "severity:<sev>", "area:<blueprint|core>") with the returned set. Missing labels are dropped from the create call and recorded on the entry state as droppedLabels[] and in the preview ledger.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a fake gh module whose label list returns { rcf-feedback, severity:major } but not area:blueprint
acceptanceCriteria.when: submit --yes is run with one pending major-severity blueprint entry
acceptanceCriteria.then: gh issue create is called with labels rcf-feedback, severity:major only; the entry state carries droppedLabels: ["area:blueprint"]

acceptanceCriteria.description: scripts/bootstrap-feedback-labels.mjs is a one-shot script a repo admin runs to create the six labels in one destination repo: rcf-feedback, severity:blocker, severity:major, severity:minor, area:blueprint, area:core. Idempotent: existing labels are left alone; missing ones are created via gh label create. The script is a maintainer aid, not called from init or doctor.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a fake gh module in the script fixture whose label list starts empty
acceptanceCriteria.when: the script is run once, then again
acceptanceCriteria.then: first run creates six labels via gh label create; second run makes zero create calls; exit 0 on both

acceptanceCriteria.description: The rendered issue title always carries the prefix ("[<effective-slug>] " for blueprints, "[rcf-lite] " for core) and the body always carries the visible rcf-feedback-fingerprint: <fp> line plus the HTML-comment twin. Both are load-bearing triage handles when labels are missing or dropped.
acceptanceCriteria.given: render() is called on a blueprint and a core entry
acceptanceCriteria.when: the rendered title and body are compared to templates
acceptanceCriteria.then: blueprint titles start with "[<slug>] "; core titles start with "[rcf-lite] "; each body carries the fingerprint on its own line and inside an HTML comment (fingerprint appears twice on purpose)

acceptanceCriteria.description: The six-label catalogue (rcf-feedback, severity:blocker, severity:major, severity:minor, area:blueprint, area:core) is exported as a single frozen constant from src/feedback/labels.js (FEEDBACK_LABELS or equivalent). Both scripts/bootstrap-feedback-labels.mjs and the submit-time label pre-check import that constant and refuse to hard-code any of the six names locally. A grep test asserts no string literal for a catalogue label name appears outside src/feedback/labels.js, its own tests, and the bootstrap script that imports it.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a fresh clone of the repo
acceptanceCriteria.when: the grep test enumerates string literals for each of the six label names across src/, scripts/, bin/
acceptanceCriteria.then: every hit is either inside src/feedback/labels.js, a test file that imports the constant, or the bootstrap script; there is no bare string literal for any of the six names elsewhere
